title: The Hollow Tithe
blurb: A toll road, a levy counted in timber, and a warden who stopped writing home.

brief.premise: a forest toll road where the levy is counted in felled timber
brief.storyline: the player is looking for a sibling who took the warden's badge and stopped writing
brief.tone: damp, wry, and short of daylight
brief.protagonist: a timber-tallier walking the road out of season

lore.title: The Hollow Tithe
lore.premise: The crown stopped asking for coin three winters ago and started asking for timber. The forest has been paying ever since, and the road that carries it is the only law out here.
lore.era: the third winter of the timber levy
lore.tone: damp, wry, and short of daylight

467299905.name: Shoulder Bottoms
467299905.blurb: Shoulder Bottoms is highland country, and keeps to itself.
ambient: The wind moves across the highland.
Somewhere off the track, an axe stops mid-stroke.
A cart has been through here recently, and heavily.
Sap has stuck your sleeve to your arm again.
The stumps beside the road are fresh, and numbered in white paint.

2259585032.name: The Warden's Shoulder
2259585032.blurb: High open ground where the road climbs out of the trees and the crown can finally see it.
2259585032.culture: Wardens, weighers and people who have learned to be elsewhere.
lore: Every cart is weighed twice on the Shoulder, and the second weight is the one that counts.
ambient: The wind up here has nothing to break it.
You can see the road for a mile in both directions, which is the point.

4222914290.name: The Long Fell
4222914290.blurb: Deep forest cut by one road and a hundred arguments about who owns the trees beside it.
4222914290.culture: Fellers and cart-drivers who count in cords and trust in writing.
lore: A cord of oak buys more here than a purse of silver.
The Compact keeps its own tally, and it does not match the crown's.
ambient: The canopy closes over the road and the light goes green.
Somewhere off the track, an axe stops mid-stroke.
Sap has stuck your sleeve to your arm again.

2150566345.description: Three roads meet under trees old enough to have opinions. Everything here smells of wet sawdust and everyone here is waiting for a cart.

npcs.name: Ilse Marrow
npcs.appearance: Broad, wind-burnt, two fingers short on her left hand and unbothered about it.
npcs.persona: Blunt, fair, and counting something the whole time she talks to you.
knows: A warden came through in autumn with a new badge and would not give a name.
The Cord House tally has been short every month since the levy doubled.
Nobody has walked the high road past the fort since the first frost.

npcs.name: Bevan Halloway
npcs.appearance: Grey, deliberate, hands scarred pale across the knuckles.
npcs.persona: Answers the question you asked and not the one you meant.
knows: He re-shod a warden's horse in autumn and was paid in crown paper, which nobody here will take.
His daughter took the road east and has not written either.

npcs.name: Sedge
npcs.appearance: Thin, cheerful, wearing three coats none of which fit.
npcs.persona: Talks to fill the silence and does not much mind what with.
knows: The weighbridge on the Shoulder gives a different number going up than coming down.
A cord of oak is worth a week's wage and worth losing a hand over.

hooks: The Cord House tally has come up short every month since the levy doubled.

2528282773.name: Stonewait
2528282773.description: A weighing station that grew walls. The road runs straight through it and stops, twice, whether you like it or not.

lock.lockedText: The Warden's Hall is shut, and the crown standard is shut in with it. Cull carries the key on him, and does not lend it.

npcs.name: Warden Cull
npcs.appearance: Neat, tired, badge polished past the point of vanity.
npcs.persona: Correct about everything and comfortable about none of it.
knows: The badge you are asking after was signed out in autumn and never signed back in.
Two tallies leave this station: one for the crown and one that is true.

npcs.name: Ott Pell
npcs.appearance: Small, ink-stained, permanently mid-sum.
npcs.persona: Would rather show you the ledger than argue with you about it.
knows: The autumn warden walked east off the road and left the horse behind.
He keeps his own copy of every weight, and he keeps it somewhere else.

hooks: A warden's badge was signed out in autumn and never signed back in.

3139050156.name: Harrowmere
3139050156.description: Where the timber finally stops being timber and starts being money. The biggest place on the road and the one least interested in the forest that pays for it.

npcs.name: Factor Odell
npcs.appearance: Comfortable, courteous, sleeves too clean for the trade he is in.
npcs.persona: Agrees with you warmly and concedes nothing.
knows: He buys crown paper at four parts in five and does not ask where it came from.
A warden sold him a full ledger in autumn and asked to be forgotten.

npcs.name: Meret Sallow
npcs.appearance: Young, precise, one sleeve permanently pushed up.
npcs.persona: Frightened of the ledger and unable to leave it alone.
knows: The Crown Yard receives more cord than the road can carry.
Somebody has been signing the difference off in a hand she recognises.

npcs.name: Auditor Vance
npcs.appearance: Travelling coat still on, a satchel she does not put down.
npcs.persona: Patient, unhurried, entirely uninterested in being liked.
knows: The assize sends somebody when a crown standard is reported light, and not before.
A weight in the hand is evidence. A story about a weight is not.

hooks: The Crown Yard takes in more timber than the road could possibly deliver.

2951464643.name: Tallyward
2951464643.description: The crown's own keep on this road: one curtain wall, one gate, and a yard that has not held a garrison in thirty years. The assize rolls are kept in the tower because there is nowhere drier.

npcs.name: Serjeant Aumbry
npcs.appearance: Grey, square, wearing a coat that fitted a larger man.
npcs.persona: Bored into precision. Answers what he is asked and not a word past it.
knows: Every weight-badge on this road is signed out of this keep and signed back into it.
The old adit south of Stonewait was a crown lead mine before the assize moved.

npcs.name: Roll-keeper Sibb
npcs.appearance: Ink to the second knuckle, spectacles pushed up and forgotten.
npcs.persona: Delighted by anybody who asks about the rolls, which nobody does.
knows: The lead for the crown standards was cut at the old adit, and the adit was shut when the seam went bad.
A weight signed out and never returned is a matter for the assize, in theory.

hooks: Nobody has audited this keep since the assize moved to Harrowmere.
The old adit is a half-morning south, and the ladders are said to still be sound.

439642358.name: the Old Adit
439642358.description: A mouth in the hillside with a lip of spoil under it, shut when the lead seam went bad. Three levels of it, and the ladders are still there.
hooks: The lead in every crown standard on this road came out of here.

arc.title: The Hollow Tithe
arc.premise: Your sister took the warden's badge, walked the road east, and stopped writing. The tally she was keeping stopped adding up at about the same time.

quest.name: Take the tally to Stonewait
quest.description: Ilse's own count is short by a cord a month. The weighing station up the high road is where the crown's number is made. Carry it there and find the warden at the gate.

beats.journal: Ilse Marrow says a warden came through in autumn with a new badge and no name, and that the Cord House tally has been short ever since.

quest.name: The two tallies of Stonewait
quest.description: Ott Pell keeps the weights and Cull keeps the key. The crown's own weight has never left the station: it is a lead disc in the Warden's Hall, and Cull has just unbarred the door for you. Look in the Hall before you go on.

beats.journal: Two tallies leave Stonewait: the crown's and the true one. The crown standard itself is in the Warden's Hall, and Cull has unbarred it.

quest.name: Follow the ledger to Harrowmere
quest.description: Ott sold his true count to Factor Odell, in Harrowmere, where the timber stops being timber and starts being money. The road runs on east. Go and read it. Take the lead standard with you; it is the only part of this nobody can argue with.

beats.journal: Ott Pell keeps the honest weights nowhere near the station. He sold the lot down the road to a factor in Harrowmere who buys paper and does not ask where it came from.
Factor Odell bought a full ledger from a warden in autumn, at four parts in five, and was asked to forget her. He remembers the hand it was written in. So do you.

quest.name: Where the lead came from
quest.description: Sibb keeps the rolls at Tallyward and has never seen the mine they describe. The old adit is south of Stonewait, in the hillside above the road. Go and look at it; she would like to know it is still there.

beats.journal: Sibb at Tallyward says the crown's lead was cut at an adit south of Stonewait. It has been shut since the seam went bad. She has never been.

quest.name: The short cord out of Kilnwait
quest.description: Bevan Halloway's carters have been paid to the short tally on every load out of Kilnwait since spring, and none of them can read the book that does it. Somebody who can should go and look at the camp.

beats.journal: The carters out of Kilnwait have been paid short for a year, and not one of them can read the ledger that says so.

quest.name: Weigh it against the crown's own
quest.description: Meret Sallow has run the beam at the Crown Yard for six years against that same standard. She will know the moment she sees it what it means.

beats.journal: Meret has weighed against a light standard for six years. Saying so costs her the beam and costs the yard nothing, which is why she never has.

quest.name: Hand the standard to the auditor
quest.description: Vance will take the weight as evidence and the assize will sit at Harrowmere. It ends the yard, the station and the warden together — and it puts your sister's hand in the roll that does it.

card.title: The Open Roll
card.subtitle: Vance takes the disc without looking at you

sections.heading: The weight
sections.body: She sets it on her own beam, which she carries, and watches it settle. Half an ounce. She writes the number down before she says anything, and what she says is that the assize will sit here within the month.

beats.journal: Vance has the standard. She will not have it quietly.

quest.name: Sell the standard to Odell
quest.description: Odell will buy the disc for the price of a year and melt it, and the road goes on exactly as it is. Nobody is named. Nobody is paid back either.

card.title: The Drawer
card.subtitle: Odell's back room, and a drawer that does not lock

sections.heading: The offer
sections.body: He does not weigh it. He turns it over once, reads the assize mark, and names a figure that is a year of anything you have ever earned. Then he puts it in a drawer that does not lock, because it does not need to.

beats.journal: Odell paid a year's money for a lump of crown lead, which tells you what it was worth to him and what it would have been worth to everybody else.

ending.title: The hand you know
ending.subtitle: read in the back room of Odell's, by one lamp

sections.heading: The ledger
sections.body: It is not the crown's book and it was never meant to be. Two columns to a page: what the road carried, and what the yard received. The second is always the larger, and the difference is always about a cord, and it has been about a cord every month since the levy doubled.

sections.heading: The hand
sections.body: Small, hard, and slanted to the left, the way she wrote everything from the time she was nine. She kept the true count for three winters, sold it to a man who buys paper and does not ask, and asked him to forget her. She did not stop writing. She stopped writing to you.

sections.heading: And now
sections.body: You know where she went and why she stopped writing, and you are holding the reason in both hands. Nobody is waiting on you. The road out of Harrowmere runs west, back the way you came, and the levy will be counted again next month whatever you do about it.

endings.title: Half an ounce
endings.subtitle: the assize sits at Harrowmere, and everybody comes

sections.heading: The finding
sections.body: The disc weighs what it weighs, and nothing anybody says survives it. Cull is suspended, the yard's beam is impounded, and the back room at Odell's is read out loud by a clerk who does not care whose hand it is in.

sections.heading: The hand
sections.body: Her name is in it eleven times, and Vance reads all eleven. Nobody in the room looks at you, which is its own kind of looking. The road will be weighed honestly from the spring, and she will not be there to see it.

endings.title: A quiet pound
endings.subtitle: Odell's back room, and the road unchanged

sections.heading: The sale
sections.body: The lead goes into the fire and comes out as nothing in particular. Odell counts the money without hurrying, because there is no hurry: the road will carry the same timber tomorrow at the same short weight.

sections.heading: The hand
sections.body: Her name stays where it is, in a book nobody will now have cause to read. You told yourself that was the point. It is even true.

endings.title: The hand you know
endings.subtitle: read in the back room of Odell's, by one lamp

sections.heading: The ledger
sections.body: It is not the crown's book and it was never meant to be. Two columns to a page: what the road carried, and what the yard received. The second is always the larger, and the difference is always about a cord, and it has been about a cord every month since the levy doubled.

sections.body: Small, hard, and slanted to the left, the way she wrote everything from the time she was nine. She kept the true count for three winters, sold it to a man who buys paper and does not ask, and asked him to forget her. She did not stop writing. She stopped writing to you.

sections.heading: And now
sections.body: You know where she went and why she stopped writing, and you are holding the reason in both hands. Nobody is waiting on you. The road out of Harrowmere runs west, back the way you came, and the levy will be counted again next month whatever you do about it.

hello.speech: Out of season and on foot. You are either lost or you are looking for somebody.

choices.text: Looking for a warden. New badge, autumn.
What is wrong with the tally here?
What is wrong with the tally here?

warden.speech: She came through, yes. Would not give a name, which around here is the same as giving one. Went up the high road toward Stonewait — that is the weighing station, north and uphill, you cannot miss it — and did not come back down.

choices.text: That is enough to go on.

tally.speech: Short. Every month since the levy doubled, and always by about a cord. I keep my own count because I am not a fool. Here — take a copy up the road and see whose face changes.

actions.description: Ilse's own count, in a small hard hand, folded twice.

hello-after.speech: You still have my count, I see. Good. It is worth more out of this house than in it.

again.speech: Back again. There is stew, and there is the other stew.

tally-again.speech: You have my count in your hand already, sir. Take it up the road to Stonewait and see whose face changes; I am not walking it for you.

hello.speech: The road is open and the weighbridge is not. State your business or use the verge.

choices.text: I am looking for a warden.

hello-tally.speech: You are carrying paper. I can always tell. Whose is it?

badge.speech: Signed out in autumn. Never signed back in. I have written it up four times and four times it has come back initialled and unread.

weights.speech: Two tallies leave this station. One goes to the crown and one is true. I sign both, which is the part I would rather you did not write down.

east.speech: Ott keeps the honest weight and Ott does not keep it here. Ask him, not me — he is on the bench inside the wall, doing sums I cannot bear to watch.

choices.text: The bench inside the wall. I will find him.

again.speech: Still here. Still open. Still not the weighbridge.

hello.speech: Paper, timber, or trouble? I buy the first, weigh the second, and price the third rather high.

choices.text: A ledger, sold to you in autumn.
Why does the Crown Yard take more cord than the road carries?

ledger.speech: A warden, yes. Four parts in five, which was generous, and she asked to be forgotten, which was cheap. I have an excellent memory and a very short one, depending.

yard.speech: Because the road is not the only way in, and the yard is not the only one counting. You did not need me to tell you that. You needed somebody to say it out loud.

price.speech: On whether the person asking is family. You have her hand about the mouth, if not the sense. It is in the back room, under the counter, and it is not for sale twice. Read it there and then decide what you are going to do about it.

choices.text: Then I will read it here.

again.speech: Back. The ledger has not moved and neither have I.

barriers.lockedText: A crown gate across the cut, barred on the far side. The station above it does not open for travellers, and there is a notice on the bar saying so.
barriers.opensText: The bar lifts. Whoever set it has been told to expect you.

item.name: Lead Standard
item.description: The crown's own weight for this station: a lead disc the size of a palm, stamped with the assize mark. Filed half an ounce light, and not recently.

entry.text: The crown standard is half an ounce light, and it was filed, not worn. Whatever is said after this, it is the thing that says it.
There is an auditor at the market stall who was not there yesterday. She is waiting for somebody and does not mind being seen waiting.
